title: Move the nine live references the retired script left behind
action: Cell ho-14 retired skills/bee-herding/scripts/control-loop.sh, but its hit list was incomplete — the orchestrator grepped four files and called the result exhaustive. A full-tree sweep found nine LIVE references still naming the deleted script in the canonical tree, and this cell moves them. Edit only skills/bee-herding/ then run the regen chain so all five mirrors carry it. THE NINE, with why each matters. references/operational-invariants.md carries SEVEN and they are the load-bearing ones: line 32 and line 53 describe the control panes' permission posture, lines 59, 82 and 106 describe the runtime-adapter seam and its per-token substitution, and line 165 describes the stop-file check. That document is what a reader consults to understand the permission split D13 protects, so pointing it at a file that no longer exists sends them looking for nothing. references/role-merge.md line 8 carries the merge-gesture command a human types. references/role-dispatch.md line 386 carries a parenthetical explaining that the control loop uses a headless invocation for CONTROL panes, which is why the WORKING agent must not — keep that contrast, it is the whole point of the sentence, and only rename the artefact. agents/openai.yaml line 3 carries the skill's short description, which is a HAND-MAINTAINED projection of SKILL.md's frontmatter description and is NOT regenerated by the regen chain; ho-14 updated the source and left this copy behind, so it is out of parity and must be brought back into it by hand. WHAT NOT TO TOUCH, and this is a hard boundary. Files under docs/history/, docs/discovery/ and plans/ also name the retired script. Those are RECORDS, not instructions: a discovery ticket saying the script used GNU timeout is a true statement about the past, and rewriting it to match the present corrupts the record. A reference is stale only when it tells a reader to do something that no longer works — never merely because its subject moved. Leave every one of them alone. ONE MORE, found by the same sweep: the Pointers section of docs/knowledge/areas/bee-herding/overview.md says the binary serves FIVE herding verbs. It now serves more — the wave, occupancy, record-worker and control-loop verbs all landed in this feature. Recount from the router rather than from memory and correct the number and the list.
verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml && .bee/bin/bee dev regen && .bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check

The permission-posture and runtime-adapter passages in operational-invariants.md name the verb, and their reasoning is unchanged.
The merge-gesture command in role-merge.md is the verb with the same role and once semantics.
The control-versus-working headless contrast in role-dispatch.md survives; only the artefact is renamed.
agents/openai.yaml's short description matches SKILL.md's frontmatter description again.
Every file under docs/history/, docs/discovery/ and plans/ that names the retired script is UNCHANGED.
The knowledge area's Pointers section states the verb count and list recounted from the router, not from memory.
artifacts: the four skill files naming the verb instead of the retired script
agents/openai.yaml back in parity with SKILL.md
the knowledge area's corrected verb count and list
key_links: agents/openai.yaml's short description and SKILL.md's frontmatter description say the same thing.
prohibitions: Do not modify any file under docs/history/, docs/discovery/ or plans/ — they are records of what was true then.
Do not hand-edit any mirrored skill tree.
Do not drop a passage's reasoning while renaming what it points at.
Do not change any production code — this cell is documentation and parity only.
Do not use bee cells cap --override-judge.
